name: Zeresh
title: Haman's wife
summary: Zeresh was the wife of Haman, the powerful advisor to King Ahasuerus (Xerxes I) in Persia. She is known from the book of Esther as the one who advised Haman to build a gallows to hang Mordecai, but later realized that Haman's plans against the Jews would lead to his downfall.

keyEvents.title: Zeresh advises Haman to build the gallows
keyEvents.description: After Haman became enraged because Mordecai refused to bow down to him, Zeresh and his friends advised him to erect a gallows fifty cubits high and ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on it.

keyEvents.title: Haman's humiliation before Mordecai
keyEvents.description: When Haman was forced to honor Mordecai publicly instead of humiliating him, he returned home in grief and told Zeresh and his friends what had happened.

keyEvents.title: Zeresh predicts Haman's downfall
keyEvents.description: Zeresh and his advisors warned Haman that if Mordecai, before whom he had begun to fall, was of Jewish descent, he would not be able to prevail against him but would certainly fall.

keyEvents.title: Haman's sons are mentioned as part of the family
keyEvents.description: Haman's ten sons, whom Zeresh bore, are mentioned in connection with the fate of the family. They were eventually killed by the Jews during their defense in Susa.

keyEvents.title: Haman executed on the gallows he built
keyEvents.description: Ironically, Haman was hanged on the same gallows that Zeresh had suggested he build for Mordecai, fulfilling her own warning about Haman's downfall.
